- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or adjust downward by 2–5% in next 3–5 days.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 70–75, forecast tends to drop; if below 65, tends to rise — adjust for 1–2% lagged momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights recent sentiment; if sentiment is high but price is falling, reduce forecast by 2–4% to avoid “sentiment-driven overcorrection.”
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.00, 0.67), model tends to misalign with true trend; use 2-period moving average of sentiment to smooth forecast bias.
